results.comment: dude, let's start with the fact that you shouldn't compare 1080 max q with the generic 1070 you sent me a link to, but the laptop version instead, okay?  Also if you saw the specs of these two, you'd notice that the clock speed is not the only difference and 1080 (max q or not) has quite a lot more CUDA cores. And considering how much fewer CUDA cores 1070 has, and how little the frequency of 1080 max q is lower in boost than that of 1070, you'd see the flaw in your logic. (in short, 1070 has indeed 12% higher clock speed in turbo, though has exactly 20% fewer cores. How can 1070 be better? + consider that 1080's memory clock is 10ghz agains 1070's 8ghz) Also, if you simply followed your own advice "look at the numbers dude" and  looked at the table Dave provided in the video at 1:32, where it clearly shows that 1080 max q is still better than 1070 laptop, you would see that what I mentioned previously is correct, while what you mentioned is wrong. Now, going further - you say that "he's getting almost 120fps on the majority of the games here" - he indeed was close to 120hz, but dude, that was 1080 max q at 1080p, and laptop gtx 1070, which is inferior, will not magically "easily" give 120 fps in 1440p in max settings if a better card doesn't give 120 fps in a smaller resolution. Another point you brought up is you 7820hk - do you really think that having your processor overclocked so much gives you extra fps? Dude, in gaming 1070 is the bottleneck in your configuration, your processor is barely even used - it's way too good for gaming, you use just a fraction of that. Turn down that overclocking, let it relax; no need to overstress it. :-) I'm saying this because most of the games I can easily stress my 1070 to the max with the cpu undervolted & undeclocked. TL;DR: Get your facts straight. (1) Laptop 1070 is NOT better than 1080 max q.
